️ APPENDIX V — The Financial Rights Of Scene Professionals

From Chapter 8. The short version.

Vendors and Makers

Market rate is determined by your costs and comparable market rates — not by what someone tells you is “normal for the scene.”

Verbal agreements are still agreements. Written ones are better.

“Exposure” is not payment unless it produces verifiable economic return that you verify independently.

The anchor price in any negotiation was set by whoever spoke first. You can reset.

Any agreement that gives someone a percentage of something whose value they control is a potential trap. Get a lawyer.

Artists and DJs

Your split is: the amount of money you receive divided by the total revenue generated.

“Pre-revenue” means nothing if the person is charging participants.

A deposit is required. Get it before the show.

A performance agreement in writing protects both parties. Insist on it.

The person who controls your booking access controls your leverage. Build two independent booking relationships.

Touring Professionals

The Venmo Note Lock: plain notes, specific windows, no vibe notes on delayed payments.

The Van Rule applies to equipment, not just supply.

The credit that accumulates across events is leverage against you.

The Five Questions Before Any Deal

1. What specifically am I giving?

2. What specifically am I receiving?

3. When specifically do I receive it?

4. Who controls the valuation of what I’m receiving?

5. What happens to my contribution if this deal falls through?

If any of these questions cannot be answered in plain language: the deal is not ready to be signed.

📖 APPENDIX W — The Institutional Betrayal Diagnostic

From Chapter 21. Is this organization betraying its members?

Signs of Institutional Betrayal

The organization says it has accountability processes. Ask:

1. Has the process ever been used?

2. Who administered the last process? Who reviews reports?

3. What was the last outcome?

4. How long do reports wait before receiving a substantive response?

5. What happens if someone reports harm about someone with institutional power?

Red Flags

Reports go to the same inbox as vendor inquiries

The safety director has three other roles and is absent during events

Mediation is offered as a substitute for investigation

The person reported continues to receive platform while the report is pending

“We can’t comment on specific personnel matters” as the entire public response

The timeline from submission to response consistently exceeds thirty days with no updates

The Parallel-Track Rule

Do not wait for institutional processes to fail before using parallel channels. Use both simultaneously from the beginning. Document both. The documentation of the institutional failure is itself evidence and advocacy.

🔁 APPENDIX Y — The Immune System Infrastructure Checklist

From Chapter 21. Annual camp and festival audit.

For Camps

The Routing Audit: Name every person we route around. Why. Since when. What formal process has addressed it.

The Roster Audit: Name every Wook in our social network. Identify my role in their operation: Flying Monkey, Validator, Bystander OG, or Camp That Knew.

The Community Compact: Do we have named norms, a named process, a named body, named consequences, and an annual review? If no: which of these is missing?

The Pathway Audit: Does our organization’s or festival’s reporting pathway function? Tested recently? Last outcome known?

The Cross-Circuit Audit: Any new members from another circuit this season? Cross-circuit check run?

The Walk-Through: Annual. Named people. Named routing. Named behavior. Named accountability process or named absence of one.

For Individuals

Have I passed information forward in the last three months?

Is there information in my possession right now that belongs to someone who needs it?

Have I made a cross-circuit check recently for anyone new in my community with a role?

Am I on the Enabler Roster for anyone? In what capacity?

Have I run the post-event behavioral scan after my last event?

Have I done the quarterly closed-door audit?

💵 APPENDIX Z — The Closing Argument

From the PLURth Angel. The whole book in one page.

The magic is real.

The scene has been making something real for fifty years. The all-night sets, the communities that form in parking lots and desert playas and warehouse basements, the connections forged in the specific conditions of deprivation and intensity and shared experience — these are real things that happen nowhere else and that have changed the lives of the people they happened to.

The magic is also being eaten.

Not by everyone. By a consistent minority with a consistent playbook, running across consistent conditions, producing consistent harm. The playbook is in this book. The conditions are in the chapters you have read. The harm is in the stories of the people who were in it.

The magic can be protected.

Not perfectly. Not by any single person. By the aggregation of boring acts done consistently by people who love the thing enough to do the boring thing. The fifteen-minute briefing. The test kit. The sealed bottle. The phone number saved in the note labeled “keep.” The subreddit response. The direct question. The printed sheet. The government name said aloud.

The boring thing is the whole magic.

The boring thing is what the magic is made of, on the back side, where nobody photographs it.

You have the flashlight.

You have the briefing.

You have the test kit.

You have the code word.

You have the five-sense ground.

You have the napkin.

You have the name.

You know what the levers are.

You know the sixteen moves the book ran on you.

You know how to crack the seal yourself.

You know how to come home.

Protect the fucking magic.
